head: The answer is not settled: a model with an attention sink and one without found the planted causes equally well
sub: Question: does less attention-sink mass make planted features easier for a sparse autoencoder to find? Not settled. A sink is attention that heads with nothing to read park on the first token. Tiny 4-layer models learned text with 64 planted causes. A sparse autoencoder at the middle layer tried to find them (recovery score, 0 to 1). Only {n_sink} of the {n_fit} models without a gate grew a sink. The slope of score on sink mass was {b}, with a 95% range of {b_lo} to {b_hi}, so it fits both a rise and a fall.
seq_lab: One test sequence. Causes {on} are on. After each trigger ▲, 3 tokens depend on them. Other tokens do not.
col_att: At token {q}, the middle layer's attention
grp2: Gather the causes in the middle layer
grp4: Gather the causes only in the last layer
same: same score, with and without a sink
foot: 4-layer transformers (about 200,000 parameters) trained 12,000 steps. Sparse autoencoder with 256 entries, 3 seeds. 1,000 test sequences · Kran Lab, Nov 8 2026
